nodes.obligation: Prove that for f in L^p of the unit interval (1 ≤ p < ∞) and h > 0, the averages f_h are continuous on [0,1] and satisfy |f_h(t)| ≤ (2h)^(-1/p) ‖f‖_p.
reader_obligations: Keep both conclusions in view: one hypothesis, f in L^p, has to deliver continuity and the quantitative bound at once.

nodes.obligation: Fix the reading of the integral: work with Lebesgue measure restricted to [0,1], so the window [t-h, t+h] contributes only its part inside [0,1]; this is the zero extension of f in disguise, and the average is the window integral divided by 2h.
reader_obligations: Understand that the problem's f, defined only on [0,1], is being read as a function on all of R that vanishes outside the interval.

nodes.obligation: From f in L^p with 1 ≤ p on a finite measure space, conclude that f is integrable.
reader_obligations: Accept that L^p on a finite measure sits inside L^1, so integrals of f are finite and the primitive below exists.

nodes.obligation: Show that the restricted measure of the window [t-h, t+h] is at most 2h, the volume of the unclipped interval.
reader_obligations: See that clipping the window to [0,1] can only shrink it, so 2h is a valid upper bound for every t.

anchors.ref: constant \((2h)^{-1}\) on an interval of length \(2h\)

nodes.obligation: Construct the primitive F(b) = integral of f over (-∞, b] for the restricted measure; F is continuous on (-∞, 1+h], so composing with t ↦ t ± h gives two continuous functions of t on [0,1].
reader_obligations: See why the half-line primitive, not the moving window, is the object to make continuous: it is a fixed function of one endpoint and needs no symmetric-difference bookkeeping.

anchors.note: The informal solution takes the symmetric-difference route; the formal proof takes the primitive route recorded here, and the dialogue question ask-1795503347-388 contrasts them.

nodes.obligation: Identify the moving window integral with the difference F(t+h) - F(t-h) of the two primitives, conclude the numerator is continuous on [0,1], and divide by the constant 2h to get continuity of the average.
reader_obligations: Check that the interval identity turns the moving integral into a difference of continuous functions, which is the only continuity input needed.

nodes.obligation: Apply Hölder on the window: the L^1 norm of f restricted to [t-h, t+h] is at most ‖f‖_p times (2h)^(1-1/p), using the window-measure bound and monotonicity of the eLpNorm under shrinking the measure.
reader_obligations: Track where each factor comes from: the exponent 1 - 1/p is Hölder's, and the 2h inside it is the window-measure bound.

nodes.obligation: Bound the norm of the window integral by its L^1 norm, divide by 2h, and combine exponents: the result is |f_h(t)| ≤ (2h)^(-1/p) ‖f‖_p. The restriction t ∈ [0,1] is never used; the bound holds for every real t.
reader_obligations: Watch the exponent arithmetic (1 - 1/p) - 1 = -1/p, and notice that no step consumed t ∈ [0,1].

nodes.obligation: Assemble the conjunction: continuity from the primitive route and the bound from the Hölder route, for every h > 0 and every 1 ≤ p < ∞.
reader_obligations: Confirm that the two conclusions were proved independently and only meet in the final conjunction.

profiles.audience: An analyst who wants the estimate and the continuity argument in the shortest correct form.
profiles.compression: State the restricted-measure reading in one clause; cite L^p ⊂ L^1 without comment; give the primitive in one line and its continuity by the standard atomless-primitive fact; state Hölder on the window and the exponent arithmetic without bookkeeping.

profiles.audience: A student who has not seen why an L^p function can be integrated against a moving window at all.
profiles.compression: Show every node; spend the most exposition on what the restricted measure means near the endpoints, on why the primitive replaces naive window-chasing, and on where each factor of the final constant comes from.

profiles.audience: A reviewer comparing the prose with the compiled Lean proof.
profiles.compression: Do not compress side conditions: name the finite-measure instance behind integrability, the NoAtoms instance behind the primitive, the interval identity, the eLpNorm lemma and monotonicity, and record that the t ∈ [0,1] binder is unused in the bound.
